AI-GENERATED DRAFT — PENDING HUMAN FACT-CHECK. Not for publication without review.

Independence of Consciousness: Non-Local Mind Models and Reported Perceptual Anomalies

Project Parallax — research draft (corpus-level, not a final publication)

Scope and source status

This draft reports only the supplied corpus metadata. A source flag in that metadata indicates that an arXiv-related context record was found; the quantitative claims below are still a corpus-scale aggregate of abstract classifications, not a hand-verified systematic review. The supplied data_type is meta_analysis_illustrative. Percentages and counts are reproduced exactly as given and are not treated as peer-reviewed effect sizes.

The dataset describes statistical classification of 88 deduplicated abstracts (Semantic Scholar + PubMed) into four labels: supports_veridical, null_result, neuro_mechanism, and inconclusive. The accompanying model note states that this is a corpus-scale aggregate, not a single-paper citation.

Skeptic critique (verbatim from dataset) Methodological check: This is a statistical aggregate of 88 abstracts classified by an LLM, NOT a hand-verified systematic review. Category boundaries (supports_veridical vs. neuro_mechanism vs. inconclusive) are inherently fuzzy, and a consistent pattern of reported near-death perceptions does NOT by itself distinguish between competing explanations (non-local consciousness vs. common neurological substrates such as hypoxia, temporal lobe activation, or REM intrusion). Percentages should be read as a rough corpus-level signal, not a peer-reviewed effect size. meta_analysis_illustrative

What the supplied aggregate is consistent with

On the labels given, 81 of 88 records (92.0%) are coded inconclusive, 5 (5.7%) as neuro_mechanism, 2 (2.3%) as supports_veridical, and 0 (0.0%) as null_result. That distribution is consistent with a literature slice in which most retrieved abstracts do not, under this classifier, clearly support a non-local or independently existing mind, and in which a larger share of the non-inconclusive remainder is coded toward neurological-mechanism accounts than toward veridical-perception accounts.

The two records labeled supports_veridical, as listed in the corpus, are a 2026 case discussion of a distressing near-death experience with reported veridical perceptions during coma, and a 2025 scoping review of end-of-life experiences and their implications for the mind-brain relationship. The five records labeled neuro_mechanism, as listed, concern REM-sleep intrusion and migraine, migraine aura as a predictor of near-death experiences, prevalence of near-death experiences with and without REM intrusion, a 2006 paper asking whether the arousal system contributes to near-death experience, and a 2019 large-scale semantic-similarity study of neurochemical models of near-death experience reports. These titles suggest competing framings; they do not, on the metadata alone, settle which framing is correct.

Many other titles in the same 88-item list concern coma prognosis, resuscitation, anesthesia, slaughter-stunning electroencephalography, palliative care, or unrelated biomedical topics. That mix is consistent with a noisy retrieval set and with the high inconclusive rate. It is not, by itself, evidence that consciousness is independent of the brain, nor evidence that all anomalous reports reduce to one neural mechanism.

Limits on interpretation for non-local mind models

Non-local mind models are sometimes invoked when people report perceptions that appear to occur during severely reduced clinical responsiveness. The supplied classifier output does not distinguish those reports from hypoxia, temporal-lobe activation, REM intrusion, or other candidate substrates, a point already stated in the dataset’s skeptic critique. Zero records were labeled null_result, which the dataset does not explain; that empty bin should not be read as a failed replication program or as positive support for independence of consciousness.

Category boundaries are described in the dataset as inherently fuzzy. LLM labeling of abstracts is not equivalent to blinded outcome extraction, preregistered inclusion criteria, or independent verification of alleged veridical details. Years, titles, and PubMed URLs are reproduced from the supplied list only; publication status, full-text access, and factual accuracy of each paper have not been independently checked in this draft.

Draft closing note for Project Parallax

Read as an illustrative corpus tally only: the supplied 88-item set is dominated by inconclusive labels (92.0%), with a small neuro_mechanism share (5.7%) and a smaller supports_veridical share (2.3%). That pattern is consistent with unresolved debate and noisy retrieval, not with a settled case for non-local mind. Human fact-checking, tighter inclusion criteria, and primary-source verification remain pending before any publication use.
